pinyin: xiōng dì xì yú qiáng, wài yù qí wǔ
literal: brothers · quarrel · in · wall, outside · resist · their · insult
natural: Brothers may quarrel inside the walls, but outside they unite against insult

meaning.en: Even people who quarrel at home join forces against an outside threat.
meaning.zh: 兄弟在家里争吵，但遇到外来侵犯时会一致对外。

equivalents: we may fight among ourselves but we stand together against outsiders

examples.zh: 两家公司平时竞争激烈，遇到行业危机却“兄弟阋于墙，外御其侮”。
examples.en: The two firms compete fiercely, but in an industry crisis they stand together.

examples.zh: “兄弟阋于墙，外御其侮”，球迷之间虽有争吵，对外却团结一致。
examples.en: Fans may quarrel, but they present a united front to outsiders.

story.en: From the Changdi ode of the Book of Songs, praising brotherhood; the saying says brothers may quarrel at home but defend each other against outsiders.
story.zh: 出自《诗经·小雅·常棣》，歌颂兄弟情谊：兄弟虽在家里争吵，却能共同抵御外侮。

date.zh: 西周初至春秋中叶 · 前11—前6世纪
date.en: early Western Zhou to mid Spring and Autumn, 11th–6th c. BC

usage.en: A quotation from the classics; formal, used to support an argument or give advice.
usage.zh: 经典引文，书面语，常用来论证或劝勉。

pinyin: jiān tīng zé míng, piān xìn zé àn
literal: hear · all · then · clear, favour · one · believe · then · dark
natural: Listen to all sides and you will see clearly; trust only one side and you will be misled

meaning.en: Considering different views leads to a sound judgement; believing only one source leads to error.
meaning.zh: 多方听取意见才能明辨是非，只听信一方就会糊涂。

equivalents: hear both sides before judging
don't believe only one source

examples.zh: 领导者要做到“兼听则明，偏信则暗”，才不会被蒙蔽。
examples.en: A leader must listen to all sides to avoid being misled.

examples.zh: 看新闻也要“兼听则明，偏信则暗”，别被单一信息误导。
examples.en: When reading the news, hear all sides and avoid being misled by a single source.

story.en: Wei Zheng told Emperor Taizong of Tang that a ruler is wise by listening widely and confused by trusting one side; the four-character form is the condensed saying.
story.zh: 魏征对唐太宗说，君主之所以明，是因为兼听；之所以暗，是因为偏信（见《资治通鉴·唐纪》），后世概括为此语。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

pinyin: fēn jiǔ bì hé, hé jiǔ bì fēn
literal: divided · long · must · unite, united · long · must · divide
natural: After long division there must be union, and after long union there must be division

meaning.en: Everything moves in cycles: union follows division and division follows union.
meaning.zh: 事物总在循环变化：分裂久了必然统一，统一久了必然分裂。

equivalents: what goes around comes around
history moves in cycles

examples.zh: 看足球联赛的格局，真是“分久必合，合久必分”。
examples.en: The shape of the football league is truly this: unity and division in turn.

examples.zh: 《三国演义》开篇就说“分久必合，合久必分”。
examples.en: The Romance of the Three Kingdoms opens by saying this line.

story.en: The famous opening of Luo Guanzhong's novel: 'The empire, long divided, must unite; long united, must divide', and then traces the fall of the Han into the Three Kingdoms.
story.zh: 《三国演义》开篇名言：“天下大势，分久必合，合久必分。”随后叙述汉末三国的分合。

date.en: late Yuan to early Ming, 14th c.

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

text: 千里马常有，而伯乐不常有
pinyin: qiān lǐ mǎ cháng yǒu, ér bó lè bù cháng yǒu
literal: thousand · li · horse · often · exist, but · Bo Le · not · often · exist
natural: Swift horses are always around, but a Bo Le, who can recognise them, is not

meaning.en: Talented people are not rare; those who can recognise and promote them are.
meaning.zh: 有才能的人并不稀少，难得的是能发现和任用人才的人。

equivalents: talent is plentiful but talent-spotters are scarce

examples.zh: 公司说缺人才，其实是“千里马常有，而伯乐不常有”。
examples.en: The company says it lacks talent, but really this line applies.

examples.zh: 他感叹自己怀才不遇，“千里马常有，而伯乐不常有”。
examples.en: He sighs that his talents go unrecognised: this line.

story.en: Han Yu's essay on horses uses the swift horse and the horse expert Bo Le as a metaphor for talented officials unrecognised by rulers.
story.zh: 韩愈《马说》以千里马和伯乐为喻，慨叹人才不被统治者识用。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

synonyms: 世有伯乐，然后有千里马

text: 士为知己者死，女为悦己者容
pinyin: shì wèi zhī jǐ zhě sǐ, nǚ wèi yuè jǐ zhě róng
literal: scholar · for · know · self · ones · die, woman · for · delight · self · ones · adorn
natural: A man will die for one who understands him; a woman adorns herself for one who delights in her

meaning.en: People give their all for those who appreciate them.
meaning.zh: 人会为理解和欣赏自己的人付出一切。

equivalents: people will do anything for those who appreciate them

examples.zh: 他对老板忠心耿耿，正是“士为知己者死，女为悦己者容”。
examples.en: He is utterly loyal to his boss: this line exactly.

examples.zh: “士为知己者死，女为悦己者容”，所以好的管理者要懂得赏识下属。
examples.en: 'A man dies for one who understands him', so good managers know how to appreciate their staff.

story.en: Yu Rang, a retainer of Zhi Bo, said it before trying to avenge his lord, whose rival had killed him: Zhi Bo had treated him as a true friend.
story.zh: 豫让为智伯报仇时所说：智伯以国士待己，故愿以死相报。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

pinyin: hǎo hǎo xué xí, tiān tiān xiàng shàng
literal: good · good · study, day · day · upward
natural: Study hard and improve every day

meaning.en: A call to work hard at your studies and make progress daily; a common slogan in Chinese schools.
meaning.zh: 勉励努力学习、每天进步；是中国学校里最常见的口号之一。

equivalents: study hard and make progress every day

examples.zh: 教室墙上贴着“好好学习，天天向上”的标语。
examples.en: The classroom wall carries the slogan 'study hard, improve every day'.

examples.zh: 妈妈对孩子说：“好好学习，天天向上”。
examples.en: Mother tells the child: study hard and improve every day.

story.en: Mao Zedong's 1951 inscription for the young people of China, which became a standard school slogan.
story.zh: 毛泽东1951年为少年儿童的题词，此后成为学校通行的口号。

usage.en: A slogan; neutral to formal, common in schools, posters and parents' encouragement.
usage.zh: 口号，常见于校园标语、海报和家长勉励。

pinyin: shī yí cháng jì yǐ zhì yí
literal: learn · foreigners' · strong · skills · in order to · control · foreigners
natural: Learn the foreigners' strengths in order to hold them in check

meaning.en: Learn the advanced technology of rivals so as to be able to resist or surpass them.
meaning.zh: 学习对手的先进技术，以便抵御或超越对方。

equivalents: learn from the enemy to beat the enemy

examples.zh: 这家企业“师夷长技以制夷”，成功打入国际市场。
examples.en: The company learned from its rivals' strengths and entered the international market.

examples.zh: 近代史课上老师讲到魏源的“师夷长技以制夷”。
examples.en: In modern history class the teacher spoke of Wei Yuan's idea.

story.en: Wei Yuan compiled the Illustrated Treatise on the Maritime Nations (1842) after the First Opium War, proposing that China learn Western military technology.
story.zh: 鸦片战争后魏源编成《海国图志》（1842），主张学习西方先进军事技术以抵御外侮。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

pinyin: dé dào duō zhù, shī dào guǎ zhù
literal: gain · the Way · much · help, lose · the Way · little · help
natural: One who has the Way gets much support; one who loses it gets little

meaning.en: A just cause wins wide support, and an unjust one is abandoned.
meaning.zh: 行事合乎正道的人得到很多人的帮助，违背正道的人则孤立无援。

equivalents: a just cause attracts support

examples.zh: 这场比赛的结果证明了“得道多助，失道寡助”。
examples.en: The result of this match proves this line.

examples.zh: 商界讲求“得道多助，失道寡助”，口碑最重要。
examples.en: In business it's 'the righteous find friends'; reputation matters most.

story.en: Mencius argues that morale and the people's hearts matter more than weather or terrain in war; whoever has the Way is helped by all.
story.zh: 孟子论战争：天时不如地利，地利不如人和，得道者多助，失道者寡助。

usage.en: A quotation from the classics; formal, used to support an argument or give advice.
usage.zh: 经典引文，书面语，常用来论证或劝勉。

variants: 得道者多助，失道者寡助

pinyin: xià chóng bù kě yǐ yù bīng
literal: summer · insect · not · can · tell · of ice
natural: You cannot talk of ice to a summer insect

meaning.en: Those limited by their experience cannot grasp what lies outside it; used about narrow-minded people.
meaning.zh: 见识受局限的人，无法理解超出自己经验的事物。

equivalents: you can't explain snow to a summer bug

examples.zh: 跟他解释这些没用，“夏虫不可以语冰”。
examples.en: It is useless explaining this to him; the saying applies.

examples.zh: “夏虫不可以语冰”，要打开眼界才能理解新事物。
examples.en: You must broaden your outlook to understand new things.

story.en: The River God (Hebo) is amazed on reaching the sea, and the Sea God Ruo tells him you cannot discuss the sea with a frog in a well or ice with a summer insect.
story.zh: 河伯见海而惊，海神若对他说：井蛙不可以语于海，夏虫不可以语于冰。

date.zh: 战国中期 · 前4—前3世纪

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

pinyin: mǎn zhāo sǔn, qiān shòu yì
literal: full · invites · loss, humble · receives · benefit
natural: Pride brings loss; modesty brings benefit

meaning.en: Arrogance leads to failure while humility leads to progress.
meaning.zh: 自满会招致损失，谦虚才能得到益处。

equivalents: pride goes before a fall
humility is the road to progress

examples.zh: 一次成功后他骄傲了，才明白“满招损，谦受益”。
examples.en: After one success he became proud and only then understood this line.

examples.zh: 校训就是“满招损，谦受益”。
examples.en: The school motto is this line.

story.en: From the Book of Documents (Shangshu), where the minister Yi advises Yu the Great that pride brings loss and modesty brings benefit — this is the way of Heaven.
story.zh: 出自《尚书·大禹谟》，伯益劝大禹：满招损，谦受益，时乃天道。

date.zh: 东晋 · 约4世纪初（伪古文《尚书》篇章）
date.en: Eastern Jin, early 4th c. (spurious “Old Text” chapter of the Book of Documents)

usage.en: A quotation from the classics; formal, used to support an argument or give advice.
usage.zh: 经典引文，书面语，常用来论证或劝勉。

pinyin: wéi fù bù rén, wéi rén bù fù
literal: become · rich · not · humane, be · humane · not · rich
natural: One who becomes rich is not humane; one who is humane does not become rich

meaning.en: Wealth is often gained at the cost of kindness; used to criticise heartless rich people.
meaning.zh: 致富的人往往不仁义，仁义的人往往不能致富；常用来批评为富不仁的人。

equivalents: wealth often comes at the expense of virtue

examples.zh: 那个黑心老板克扣工资，真是“为富不仁，为仁不富”。
examples.en: That heartless boss docks wages, exactly this line.

examples.zh: “为富不仁，为仁不富”，这话虽然绝对，却点出了某些现象。
examples.en: This line is absolute, but it points to a real phenomenon.

story.en: Mencius quotes Yang Huo's saying '为富不仁矣，为仁不富矣' (with the particle 矣) in a discussion on land taxes; he does not endorse it but cites it as a warning.
story.zh: 孟子在论井田与税制时引阳虎之言“为富不仁矣，为仁不富矣”，作为警戒（原文有“矣”字）。

usage.en: A quotation from the classics; formal, used to support an argument or give advice.
usage.zh: 经典引文，书面语，常用来论证或劝勉。

pinyin: wú xiàn fēng guāng zài xiǎn fēng
literal: boundless · scenery · on · perilous · peak
natural: The finest views are on the most dangerous peaks

meaning.en: The greatest rewards lie in difficult and risky places; only those who dare to climb reach them.
meaning.zh: 最美的风光在艰险的山峰，只有敢于攀登的人才能看到；比喻成就在于克服困难。

equivalents: no pain, no gain
the best views come from the hardest climbs

examples.zh: 创业就是“无限风光在险峰”，风险越大回报越大。
examples.en: Starting a business is just this: the higher the risk the greater the reward.

examples.zh: 登山队员把“无限风光在险峰”写在旗帜上。
examples.en: The mountaineers wrote this line on their flag.

origin.source: 毛泽东《七绝·为李进同志题所摄庐山仙人洞照》

story.en: Mao Zedong wrote this poem in 1961 for a photograph by Li Jin of the Immortal Cave on Mount Lu.
story.zh: 毛泽东1961年为李进拍摄的庐山仙人洞照片题诗。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

text: 瓜田不纳履，李下不整冠
pinyin: guā tián bù nà lǚ, lǐ xià bù zhěng guān
variants: 瓜田不纳履，李下不正冠
literal: melon · field · not · put on · shoes, plum · under · not · adjust · cap
natural: Don't stoop to put on your shoes in a melon field, or adjust your cap under a plum tree

meaning.en: Avoid doing anything that might look suspicious, even if innocent.
meaning.zh: 避免做容易引起嫌疑的事，即使无心也要小心。

equivalents: avoid even the appearance of wrongdoing
be above suspicion

examples.zh: 官员与企业家交往要注意“瓜田不纳履，李下不整冠”。
examples.en: Officials dealing with businesspeople must heed this line.

examples.zh: 为了避嫌，他“瓜田不纳履，李下不整冠”，从不收客户的礼物。
examples.en: To avoid suspicion he never accepts gifts from clients.

story.en: From the ancient Yuefu poem 'Conduct of a Gentleman': 'a gentleman forestalls trouble and does not stay in suspicious places; in a melon field do not put on your shoes, under a plum tree do not straighten your cap' (some texts read 李下不正冠).
story.zh: 出自乐府古辞《君子行》：“君子防未然，不处嫌疑间。瓜田不纳履，李下不正冠。”（亦作“整冠”）

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

text: 疾风知劲草，烈火见真金
pinyin: jí fēng zhī jìng cǎo, liè huǒ jiàn zhēn jīn
literal: fierce · wind · reveals · strong · grass, blazing · fire · shows · true · gold
natural: Strong winds reveal the sturdy grass; blazing fire shows true gold

meaning.en: Hard times reveal who is truly strong, loyal or genuine.
meaning.zh: 危难考验才能显出谁是真正坚强可靠的人。

equivalents: a friend in need is a friend indeed
adversity reveals true character

examples.zh: 这次灾难让我们看到了谁是真朋友，“疾风知劲草，烈火见真金”。
examples.en: The disaster showed us who our true friends are: this line.

examples.zh: “疾风知劲草，烈火见真金”，困难时刻才见人品。
examples.en: Character shows in hard times.

story.en: Emperor Guangwu of Han told his general Wang Ba, who stayed loyal when others deserted: 'only in strong winds do you know the sturdy grass'. The second half was added in later folk usage.
story.zh: 光武帝对忠心不二的王霸说：“疾风知劲草。”后人又添“烈火见真金”对举。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

synonyms: 路遥知马力，日久见人心

pinyin: zhī qí bù kě ér wéi zhī
literal: know · it · cannot · yet · do · it
natural: Knowing it cannot be done, yet doing it anyway

meaning.en: To persist in a worthy cause despite little chance of success; sometimes used as criticism of stubbornness.
meaning.zh: 明知不可能成功仍要去做；多形容坚持理想的精神，有时也含批评固执之意。

equivalents: fight on though the odds are against you
tilt at windmills

examples.zh: 他明知胜算不大，却“知其不可而为之”，坚持参赛。
examples.en: He knew the odds were poor yet pressed on and entered the contest.

examples.zh: 孔子被人称作“知其不可而为之”的人。
examples.en: Confucius was described as a person who tried in spite of the odds.

story.en: A gatekeeper at Shimen described Confucius as 'the one who knows it cannot be done and yet does it'.
story.zh: 石门的守门人评论孔子：“是知其不可而为之者与？”

usage.en: A quotation from the classics; formal, used to support an argument or give advice.
usage.zh: 经典引文，书面语，常用来论证或劝勉。

pinyin: qiè gōu zhě zhū, qiè guó zhě hóu
variants: 窃钩者诛，窃国者为诸侯
literal: steal · belt-hook · ones · executed, steal · state · ones · made marquis
natural: He who steals a belt-hook is executed; he who steals a state becomes a lord

meaning.en: Small thieves are punished while great ones are honoured; a protest against injustice.
meaning.zh: 偷小东西的人被处死，窃取国家的人却封侯，讽刺社会不公。

equivalents: hang the petty thief and crown the big one

examples.zh: 看到大贪官逍遥法外，人们感叹“窃钩者诛，窃国者侯”。
examples.en: Seeing a big embezzler go free, people sighed this line.

examples.zh: 历史学家引用“窃钩者诛，窃国者侯”评论权力与法律。
examples.en: The historian quoted this line to comment on power and law.

story.en: Zhuangzi (Quqie) says that one who steals a hook is executed while one who steals a state becomes a lord. Sima Qian quotes the saying in his Biographies of the Wandering Knights in the form 窃钩者诛，窃国者侯.
story.zh: 《庄子·胠箧》有“彼窃钩者诛，窃国者为诸侯”；《史记·游侠列传》引作“窃钩者诛，窃国者侯”。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

pinyin: jīng chéng suǒ zhì, jīn shí wéi kāi
literal: sincerity · where · reaches, metal · stone · become · open
natural: Where sincerity reaches, even metal and stone will open

meaning.en: With sincere, wholehearted effort, even the hardest obstacles can be overcome.
meaning.zh: 真诚专一到了极点，连金石也会被感动而裂开；比喻只要诚心努力，什么困难都能克服。

equivalents: where there's a will there's a way
sincerity can move mountains

examples.zh: 他十年如一日地寻找失散的女儿，终于“精诚所至，金石为开”。
examples.en: For ten years he searched for his lost daughter and in the end this line proved true.

examples.zh: “精诚所至，金石为开”，只要诚心，就会有结果。
examples.en: If you are sincere, you will get a result.

story.en: Source: Biography of Prince Si of Guangling in the Book of the Later Han, which reads 精诚所加，金石为开; the form with 所至 is the common one (Li Guang's arrow in the stone is a related story).
story.zh: 《后汉书·广陵思王荆传》作“精诚所加，金石为开”；“所至”为通行说法（与李广射石的传说相关）。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

pinyin: tīng qí yán ér guān qí xíng
literal: listen · his · words · and · watch · his · deeds
natural: Listen to what a person says and watch what he does

meaning.en: Judge someone not just by words but by actions.
meaning.zh: 判断一个人不能只听他说什么，还要看他做什么。

equivalents: actions speak louder than words
judge by deeds, not words

examples.zh: 招人时要“听其言而观其行”，不能只看简历。
examples.en: When hiring, listen and watch conduct; don't rely on the CV alone.

examples.zh: 交朋友贵在“听其言而观其行”。
examples.en: In making friends, it is important to watch deeds as well as listen to words.

story.en: Confucius said: 'At first I listened to what people said and trusted their conduct; now I listen to what they say and watch what they do'; he changed after Zai Yu slept in the daytime.
story.zh: 孔子因宰予昼寝而感慨：“始吾于人也，听其言而信其行；今吾于人也，听其言而观其行。”

usage.en: A quotation from the classics; formal, used to support an argument or give advice.
usage.zh: 经典引文，书面语，常用来论证或劝勉。

pinyin: gǒu fù guì, wù xiāng wàng
literal: if · rich · noble, don't · mutually · forget
natural: If one of us becomes rich and powerful, let us not forget each other

meaning.en: A pledge among old friends not to forget one another on getting rich.
meaning.zh: 约定谁先富贵了，不要忘记一同受苦的朋友。

equivalents: don't forget your friends when you make it

examples.zh: 创业之初，几个兄弟说好“苟富贵，勿相忘”。
examples.en: When they started the business the brothers promised each other this line.

examples.zh: 发达之后，他早把“苟富贵，勿相忘”忘了。
examples.en: After getting rich he forgot this pledge.

story.en: Chen Sheng, a hired farmhand, said it to his fellow workers before he led the first big uprising against the Qin; they laughed, and he replied with 'how can sparrows know the swan's ambition'.
story.zh: 陈涉年轻时与人佣耕，对同伴说此话，同伴笑他，他答以“燕雀安知鸿鹄之志哉”。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

text: 虚心使人进步，骄傲使人落后
pinyin: xū xīn shǐ rén jìn bù, jiāo ào shǐ rén luò hòu
literal: empty · heart · makes · people · advance, pride · makes · people · fall behind
natural: Modesty helps people make progress; pride makes them fall behind

meaning.en: Be humble and keep learning, because arrogance holds you back.
meaning.zh: 虚心让人不断进步，骄傲自满则使人落后。

equivalents: modesty leads to progress and pride to decline

examples.zh: 班主任常说“虚心使人进步，骄傲使人落后”，要我们保持谦虚。
examples.en: The class teacher often says this to keep us modest.

examples.zh: 拿了奖，他提醒自己“虚心使人进步，骄傲使人落后”。
examples.en: After winning the prize he reminded himself of this line.

origin.source: 毛泽东《中国共产党第八次全国代表大会开幕词》

story.en: From Mao Zedong's opening speech at the Eighth National Congress of the Communist Party of China in 1956.
story.zh: 出自毛泽东1956年在中共八大上的开幕词。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。

pinyin: yán bì xìn, xíng bì guǒ
literal: words · must · be true, deeds · must · bear fruit
natural: Be true to one's word and carry out one's deeds to completion

meaning.en: Keep your promises and see through what you do.
meaning.zh: 说话一定守信用，做事一定坚决果断。

equivalents: be as good as your word

examples.zh: 做生意要“言必信，行必果”，才能赢得客户的信任。
examples.en: In business you must keep your word and follow through to earn clients' trust.

examples.zh: 他向来“言必信，行必果”，答应的事一定做到。
examples.en: He always keeps his word and does what he promises.

story.en: Confucius, asked what makes a scholar-official, says that one who is true in word and resolute in action is of a lesser rank — a small-minded but reliable man.
story.zh: 子贡问何谓士，孔子答“言必信，行必果，硁硁然小人哉”，意为信守诺言而略显固执。

usage.en: A quotation from the classics; formal, used to support an argument or give advice.
usage.zh: 经典引文，书面语，常用来论证或劝勉。

pinyin: shí shí wù zhě wéi jùn jié
literal: recognise · the times · ones · are · outstanding · figures
natural: Those who understand the times are the outstanding ones

meaning.en: A wise person adapts to circumstances; sometimes used with a hint of opportunism.
meaning.zh: 能认清形势、顺应潮流的人才是杰出人物；有时带有见风使舵的意味。

equivalents: a wise man adapts to the times

examples.zh: “识时务者为俊杰”，公司转型时他第一个转了方向。
examples.en: 'The wise adapt to the times': he was the first to change direction when the company transformed.

examples.zh: 面对大势，不如“识时务者为俊杰”。
examples.en: Faced with the trend, it is better to read the times.

origin.source: 《三国志·蜀书·诸葛亮传》裴松之注引《襄阳记》

story.en: Pei Songzhi's note quotes the Xiangyang Ji: Sima Hui told Liu Bei that ordinary scholars do not understand the times, but 'those who understand the times are outstanding', pointing to Zhuge Liang and Pang Tong.
story.zh: 裴注引《襄阳记》：司马徽对刘备说儒生俗士不识时务，“识时务者在乎俊杰”，指诸葛亮、庞统。

usage.en: A quoted line; literary, common in essays, captions, speeches and everyday quotation.
usage.zh: 引用的名句，书面语，常见于作文、文案、演讲和日常引用。
